title: Seclusion on the mountain
hookLine: he retreats to Hira for days, taking provisions, praying in the way of Ibrahim (Bukhari)

lines: A BAG OF FOOD, PACKED AT HOME.
cards: A bag of food, packed at home. That's where today's story begins. A man fills a bag with provisions, says goodbye to his wife, and walks out of the city and up a mountain.
He stays up there for nights at a time. When the food runs out, he comes home, and she packs the bag again. A new part of the sirah opens here, the revelation, and it opens with a packed lunch.

teach.b: The hadith is in Sahih al-Bukhari, told by 'Aishah. Before revelation, she says, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ began to see dreams that came true like the break of dawn. Then solitude was made dear to him.
He went to the cave of Hira and did tahannuth there, and a gloss inside the hadith explains the word: worship, for a number of nights, before he returned to his family.
He took provisions for the stay, then came back to Khadijah, and she gave him provisions for the same again. Two halves: alone on the mountain, and a household at the bottom of it.
The seclusion wasn't an escape from Khadijah; she was the one keeping it going, bag after bag. Now the word.
Ibn Hisham, who edited Ibn Ishaq's biography, adds a note: the Arabs said tahannuth and tahannuf alike, meaning the hanifiyyah, the way of the hanif.

That's the word from day seven hundred two, the hanifs, who turned from the idols toward the God of Ibrahim. So some readers hear in his retreat the old way of Ibrahim, kept by a few seekers. What did he pray?
The sources don't say. They give us where, and how long, and the food. And the habit stayed.
Sahih al-Bukhari records that later, every Ramadan, he spent the last ten days in the mosque in i'tikaf, a retreat for worship, until the end of his life.
I'tikaf is still kept in mosques today.

how: Muslims keep i'tikaf, a retreat for worship in the mosque, especially in the last ten days of Ramadan, following the Prophet's ﷺ practice recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari.

games.q: the food you carried up the mountain is gone. you want to keep praying alone. what do you do?
o: stay and fast until you're done.
go home, and let Khadijah pack the bag again.
games.why: he came back to Khadijah, and she gave him provisions for the same again. the retreat ran on a household.

practice: Sit a little apart, even just for now, and let the room go quiet around you. If you pray, pray here, alone with the one; if not, simply stay with the quiet.
Then remember who keeps things running so you can have it, your own Khadijah with the bag.

wordCard.voice: Tahannuth. Worship in seclusion, night after night, as he did in the cave of Hira, carried by provisions from home. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: worship in seclusion; Ibn Hisham links it to tahannuf, the way of the hanif.

carryVoice: Your line: alone with the one. And somebody packing the bag at home. Day seven hundred twenty-two.
